sections.h1: Most blockchain proposals do not need a blockchain
lead: Before a ledger earns a place in your architecture, someone has to ask what a database cannot do here. We start with that question, and sometimes the answer is to build something simpler.

sections.h2: Blockchain Consulting & Integration: what is included

p: A written view on whether a shared ledger fits the problem, who the participants are and what trust gap it closes.
Public, permissioned or hybrid networks compared on cost, privacy, throughput and the skills your team has.
Connecting on-chain components to ERP, payments, identity and data platforms so the ledger does not become an island.
A narrow, time-boxed build that tests the riskiest assumption first, with exit criteria agreed in advance.
Who runs nodes, who approves changes, and what happens when a participant leaves.
If you proceed, the work passes to build teams in smart contracts, tokenisation or custom software.
Identify the process, the parties and the failure that costs you money today.
Compare a ledger against simpler options on the same criteria.
Pick a network and design the integration points.
Build a proof of concept and measure it against the criteria set at the start.
Scale, change course or stop. A stop is a valid result.
If the review shows a conventional system does the job, the report says so, and that is the end of the engagement.

faq.q: How do we know if we need a blockchain?
a: Several parties who do not fully trust each other must share and update the same records, and no single party should control them. If that is not your situation, a database is usually better.

faq.q: Can you integrate with our ERP?
a: Yes. Integration with ERP, payment and identity systems is a core part of the work, not an afterthought.

faq.q: How long does a proof of concept take?
a: It depends on scope, which we fix at the start. A proof of concept should be small enough to answer one question.

faq.q: Do you also build the production system?
a: Yes, through our smart contract, tokenisation and custom software teams, if the proof of concept justifies it.
